recap.text: Donut opens three boxes in the personal space. The bronze one holds an expired tube of mace for a keychain. The gold one holds their first snare card, a very rare consumable called Hobbled, its face a pair of legs tied together. It cuts a totem's summoning time by ninety per cent, so a minute becomes six seconds. Carl puts it in their first eighteen-card deck anyway, for realism.

beats.headline: The first snare card
beats.text: Back in the personal space, Donut opens three boxes. The bronze Stranger Danger box holds an expired tube of mace for a keychain, a joke prize with no magic at all. The gold T'Ghee box, earned for using the practice room, holds a single card: their first snare card, a very rare consumable called Hobbled, its face a pair of legs tied together. It cuts a totem's summoning time by ninety per cent, and if the totem times out and is pulled again, the cut persists through combat. A minute becomes six seconds. Too bad the card is consumable.
beats.gist: Donut opens three boxes and finds Hobbled, a card that cuts a totem's summoning time ninety per cent.

beats.headline: Into the practice deck
beats.text: Carl and Donut put together their first eighteen-card deck: six totems, six utility cards, three snares, two mystics and a single Flee card. The snares are pointless in a practice simulation, because they only work against an opponent carrying cards, but Carl wants a realistic deck, since a fight does not always give warning. Hobble, consumable, goes in with the mana-draining Hole in the Bag and the new Damnation card.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut build an eighteen-card practice deck, adding Hobble, a snare, for realism despite its uselessness.
